status.label: Profile preview blocking and ownership
status.detail: The author supplied a report and a 30 GB extraction scenario; the later font-file lock may involve a different handler.

next_action.label: Compare handlers under disk load
next_action.reason: Determine which registered preview handler blocks before attributing Explorer scheduling or font locking to PowerToys.

judgment.rationale: The author answered 'all previewers', supplied diagnostics and described a concrete large-extraction comparison. A maintainer can test this without another generic evidence request, but the asserted foreground-thread explanation is not confirmed.
evidence: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/32571#issuecomment-2128970472 describes selecting files with preview enabled during 30 GB archive extraction in another Explorer window.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/32571#issuecomment-2129059015 says separate-folder processes did not prevent the stall.
The final comment describes a copied font file remaining locked by preview; PowerToys' preview module list has no dedicated font preview handler.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the disk-load scenario with known PowerToys and built-in handlers, profile the blocked process and separately identify the font lock owner.

fix_assessment.rationale: A cancellable preview/lifetime correction is plausible only for an identified PowerToys handler. Generic Explorer load and the font handler must not be assigned to PowerToys without measurement.

proposed_fixes.title: Bound preview work and release obsolete preview resources
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a handler's synchronous initialization/rendering or stale preview resources block selection under heavy I/O. The font-file lock could be a separate built-in-handler lifetime issue; a common PowerToys root cause is not established.
plan: Identify the registered handler and blocked process for a selected PowerToys-supported file while reproducing the archive-extraction load; compare preview disabled and a built-in handler.

Trace the confirmed PowerToys handler through src/modules/previewpane and its DoPreview/Unload boundary. Measure parsing, rendering and resource release instead of assuming Explorer and rendering share one foreground thread.
If confirmed, move only safe expensive parsing off the handler UI path with bounded cancellation, marshal UI/COM operations correctly and cancel obsolete generations when selection changes.

Verify that Unload releases handler-specific streams/resources; existing common FormHandlerControl.Unload already disposes child controls, so do not claim cleanup is universally absent. Route a separately owned font lock to its actual handler.
verification: During the 30 GB extraction comparison, Explorer selection remains responsive and stale previews never replace the current selection.
After selecting another file or closing preview, copying/deleting test files is possible when no application intentionally owns them.
Compare handlers and disk-load baselines so disk contention alone is not misreported as a PowerToys regression.

confidence.rationale: There is a concrete stress scenario but no blocked-thread trace or handler attribution yet.

issue_context.summary: Explorer preview delays file selection during heavy archive extraction; a later report also describes a font-file lock after copying.
known_information: A diagnostic ZIP and an 'all previewers' answer are already present.
The 30 GB extraction occurs in a different Explorer window, with separate-process folder launching enabled.
The report does not identify a specific preview handler or confirm its blocked thread.
The live issue remains an open, unassigned bug despite its original enhancement-form wording.
inferences: I/O contention, handler work and Explorer synchronization are competing causes.
The font example is not sufficient to prove ownership by a PowerToys handler.
issue_context.analysis: The next uncertainty is maintainer profiling and ownership, not a repeated reporter checklist. Use the supplied stress sequence with controlled file types and a preview-off baseline.
initial_investigation: Read the report and all seven comments.
Checked the issue timeline; no concrete linked fix is exposed.

Inspected current upstream previewpane handler directories and common controls: IPreviewHandlerControl defines DoPreview/Unload and FormHandlerControl.Unload already disposes controls; no dedicated font preview handler is listed.

reproduce.title: Preview responsiveness and lock ownership
reproduce.version_requirement: Record a current PowerToys build and Windows version; the original post does not supply a version.
prerequisites: An isolated test volume with sufficient space for both a 30 GB archive and extraction output
Known PowerToys-supported preview samples and a legally usable test font
Existing user files must not be used for deletion tests.
reproduce.setup_prompt: In a dedicated project test-data directory, prepare an approximately 30 GB ZIP/extraction workload and small valid SVG/Markdown samples. Verify available disk capacity first, do not alter existing files, document cleanup, and include a legally available test font only if already present. Do not perform deletion tests on user data.
steps: 1. Record the actual registered preview handler for each sample.
2. In one Explorer window extract the large test archive; in another enable preview and rapidly change selection among the small samples.
3. Compare preview disabled and built-in-handler samples while capturing the blocked process/thread and elapsed selection time.
4. Separately copy the test font, select it with preview enabled, change selection and attempt deletion; identify the holding process rather than assuming it is PowerToys.
reproduce.expected_result: Selection is responsive, obsolete previews cancel and resources release on unload; identify separately owned stalls or locks.

actions.label: Review handler-specific responsiveness plan
actions.note: Confirm PowerToys ownership and the blocked boundary before changing threading or stream lifetime.
